newsitem.title: CANADA: Merger of Canada's Avenor and Repap put in doubt.
newsitem.headline: Merger of Canada's Avenor and Repap put in doubt.

text.p: Canadian pulp and paper concern Avenor Inc.'s planned C$2.6 billion ($1.9 billion) acquisition of Repap Enterprises Inc. was put in doubt on Monday after Canada's largest pension fund gave the deal a thumbs down.

Officials at Quebec public pension fund manager Caisse de depot et placement, which holds a 10 percent stake in Avenor, told reporters they were unhappy with the C$3.2 billion ($2.3 billion) of debt the merged entity would carry.
The Caisse said that other institutional holders indicated they would also vote against the merger.
Complicating the picture was news on Monday that Avenor rejected a friendly offer by pulp and paper rival Domtar Inc. to merge with it and Repap.

"I would think that it's pretty unlikely that they (Avenor) would get the vote (from shareholders) because somebody else has approached them and is interested in buying them," said a New York-based arbitrager.
Repap's shares fell C23 cents to C$2.19 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday, underlining the market's doubts about the merger.
Avenor shares closed up C$1.45 at C$24 in Toronto, while Domtar fell C15 cents to C$11.45.
The merger of Avenor and Repap, both Montreal-based pulp and paper companies, was due to close if shareholders approved it on Wednesday. But it has met with significant shareholder resistance.
Avenor earlier this month cut its stock and debt offer to one Avenor share for every eight Repap shares and excluded Repap's British Columbia operations from the deal.
The original bid was one Avenor share for every 4.25 Repap shares, plus the assumption of C$2.4 billion ($1.7 billion) in debt.
In separate statements on Monday, Avenor and Domtar said Domtar last week asked Avenor to consider a merger, preferably before the shareholder vote on the Avenor-Repap deal.

"We had hoped that, by adding Domtar's complementary businesses, management and strong balance sheet to this mix, we would have allayed the concerns of Avenor's shareholders," Domtar Chief Executive Raymond Royer said.
Avenor said it rebuffed Domtar so it could focus on the Repap merger, but did not rule out talking to Domtar later.
Avenor Chief Financial Officer Denis Aubin told Reuters he did not feel that Domtar would make a hostile bid.
